title: Prana: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Prana is breath and vitality in yoga and Ayurveda. It is a traditional category, not a measured gas and not a supplement.

quick_answer.question: What does Prana mean?
quick_answer.answer: Prana means breath and a vitality those traditions treat as more than air. Practices that use the word do not thereby prove a life-force substance.

intro: Prana covers breath and life. English energy is the usual loose translation and the usual place the meaning slips.

sections.heading: What does Prana mean?
sections.content:
Yoga regulates it in pranayama. Ayurveda speaks of it in relation to vitality and routine. The two are neighbors, not one diagram. Britannica's article is a short orientation. Forceful breathing can make you dizzy without confirming the cosmology.

The neighboring page is [what prana is](/articles/what-is-prana/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
Hatha texts add techniques and cautions. Apps add timers and product language. The question page stays with how traditions describe the word. Nadis are the channels in some maps.

A wider map lives at the [breathwork topic](/topics/breathwork/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
Watch the breath if you want an attention practice. Study the word if you want the tradition. Do not buy a product said to increase prana. Ask a clinician before intense breath retention if you have heart or lung disease.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [how traditions describe it](/questions/how-do-traditions-describe-prana/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not equate prana with oxygen. Do not use the word to sell a detox. Tingling is not a credential.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Prana has a traditional job that popular English often widens.
Context decides which school is speaking.
This entry defines the word and points to a longer page.

faq.question: Is Prana a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. Oxygen is chemistry. Prana is a traditional category that includes breath and more than breath.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the explainer and the breathwork pillar.
